us-chase.conditions: Domestic case: a student living in New Haven keeps a Chase account with a US address with no special condition. Published policy for a customer who later moves abroad (Deposit Account Agreement, sec. G 'Change of Address'): 'You must promptly notify us of any change in the address(es) associated with your account. If you change your address to an address located outside the United States, or we determine that you are residing outside the United States, we may close your account.' So for a customer living abroad, keeping the account is conditional and at Chase's discretion. The bank-initiated closure clause (sec. VIII 'Closing Your Account'): 'Either you or we may close your account at any time for any reason or no reason without prior notice.' The agreement also says ACH/RTP may not be used on behalf of someone who is not a US resident.
us-chase.usResidentPolicy: Not applicable as a restriction: Chase is a US bank and US persons are its main customers. It collects a TIN, which for a US person means a W-9 SSN/ITIN. The restriction runs the other way: foreign addresses and foreign residence can lead to closure (see conditions).

abroad.card: Foreign Exchange Rate Adjustment: 3% of the purchase amount after conversion to US dollars, for card purchases, non-ATM cash or ATM withdrawals in a currency other than USD (Additional Banking Services and Fees, eff. 6/14/2026). Chase Sapphire Banking and Private Client waive it.
abroad.atm: $5 per withdrawal at a non-Chase ATM outside the US and US territories, plus the 3% Foreign Exchange Rate Adjustment on foreign-currency withdrawals, plus any ATM-owner surcharge.
abroad.outgoing: Consumer Online USD International Wire (chase.com or Chase Mobile): $40 per transfer. Consumer Online FX International Wire (sent in foreign currency): $5 per transfer, or $0 if the amount is $5,000 USD or more. A banker-assisted international wire in USD or FX costs $50.
abroad.incoming: Domestic and International Incoming Wire: $15 per transfer, or $0 if the wire was originally sent with the help of a Chase banker or using chase.com/Chase Mobile.
abroad.fxMargin: 'For wire transfers you send or we receive in a foreign currency, the exchange rate is determined by us in our sole discretion and includes a spread ... You should expect that these foreign exchange rates will be less favorable than rates quoted online or in publications.' Card transactions use the network rate plus the 3% adjustment fee. No margin percentage is published for wires.
abroad.days: not published (Chase gives an availability date in the remittance-transfer disclosure at the time of sending)
abroad.opening: Chase's guidance for non-residents and international students says a passport is accepted as primary ID. It also says 'Proof of U.S. address must be provided', and that someone without an SSN can use an ITIN. Chase's international-student page says that without an SSN 'you'll need to visit a branch and bring a current passport, proof of U.S. address and secondary identification (i.e. driver's license, state-issued ID, or Form I-20).' In practice this means an in-branch opening in the US with a US address. Chase publishes no remote opening for someone who lives abroad.
abroad.kyc: Account opening follows the CIP rule (31 CFR 1020.220): name, date of birth, a residential street address, and an ID number. That number is a TIN for a US person, or for a non-US person a TIN, passport number with country of issuance, alien ID number, or another government photo ID number. Chase accepts a valid TIN (SSN/ITIN). A US person gives a W-9 SSN. A nonresident alien (e.g. an F-1 student under the substantial presence test exemption) gives a W-8BEN. The Deposit Account Agreement requires prompt notice of address changes. Chase publishes no specific KYC-refresh cycle.
abroad.taxAtSource: US federal: 0% on bank deposit interest paid to a nonresident alien when it is not effectively connected with a US trade or business (IRC 871(i)(2)(A); IRS 'Nontaxable types of interest income for nonresident aliens'). The NRA must give the bank a valid W-8BEN, otherwise backup withholding (24%) or 30% withholding can apply. Deposit interest of $10 or more is reported on Form 1042-S (income code 29) when the NRA lives in a country listed in Rev. Proc. 2024-42.

assumptions: SLATE assumes a Chase customer who moves abroad keeps the account only until Chase acts on the foreign address, which the agreement allows it to do at any time and without notice. SLATE does not model a fixed grace period, because none is published.
SLATE assumes the 3% Foreign Exchange Rate Adjustment applies to the standard Chase Total Checking account. Premium tiers that waive it are not modelled.

us-bank-of-america.conditions: Domestic case: kept with no special condition while the student lives in New Haven. For a customer who later moves abroad, the Deposit Agreement and Disclosures (eff. May 15, 2026) has no clause that closes accounts because of a foreign address. It does contain the general power to 'convert your account to another type of account, revoke privileges or close your account ... when we consider it appropriate or necessary', and it binds customers to OFAC sanctions rules. BofA publishes a page for international customer service (calling from abroad) but no 'moving abroad' FAQ. So retention abroad is not restricted on paper and depends on the general closure discretion. The bank-initiated closure clause: 'You or we may close your checking or savings account at any time without advance notice.'
us-bank-of-america.usResidentPolicy: Not applicable as a restriction (US bank). Deposit Agreement, 'Tax Information': the customer certifies the SSN/TIN and backup-withholding status. 'If you are a certified nonresident individual ... you must renew your status prior to the end of the third calendar year following the year in which you last certified ... If you become a U.S. citizen or resident for U.S. tax purpose after opening your account, you must notify us within 30 days and provide us with your certified name and TIN.' BofA also states that it complies with FATCA.

abroad.card: International Transaction Fee: 3% of the US dollar amount for a transaction in a foreign currency, and $0 for a transaction in US dollars. Waived for the BofA Rewards Premier tier (Personal Schedule of Fees, eff. Aug 7, 2026).
abroad.atm: Non-Bank of America ATM fee in a foreign country: $5.00 per withdrawal or transfer, plus the 3% International Transaction Fee on foreign-currency cash, plus any ATM-operator fee. The fee 'do[es] not apply at some ATMs located outside the United States' (Global ATM Alliance-type partners; BofA says to call before travel).
abroad.outgoing: International outgoing wire in US dollars: $45. International outgoing wire in foreign currency: 'No wire fee, but exchange rate markups apply.' Personal Schedule of Fees, eff. Aug 7, 2026.
abroad.incoming: International incoming wire: $15. Waived for BofA Rewards Preferred Plus, Preferred Honors and Premier tiers.
abroad.fxMargin: 'There are markups associated with the currency conversion included in our exchange rate and we make money from the foreign currency exchange. Exchange rates are determined by Bank of America at its sole discretion.' The Deposit Agreement applies an 'all-in exchange rate' that 'may include profit, fees, costs, charges or other mark ups'. No margin percentage is published.
abroad.days: not published
abroad.opening: BofA's international-student page sets the eligibility as 'You have a physical address where you reside' and 'You are not a U.S. citizen'. A nonresident alien must give a physical foreign address and a US mailing address, two unexpired IDs (primary: foreign passport, with or without a US visa), and a tax ID if applicable (foreign TIN, SSN or ITIN). Opening is by appointment at a financial center, in person. Citizens of sanctioned countries must provide proof of US residency. BofA publishes no remote opening for someone who is still abroad.
abroad.kyc: CIP (31 CFR 1020.220) at opening. US persons certify an SSN/TIN (W-9). A nonresident alien certifies foreign status (W-8BEN) and must renew it before the end of the third calendar year after the last certification. If it lapses by the last day of the fourth year, interest becomes subject to backup or FATCA withholding. A customer who becomes a US citizen or tax resident must notify BofA within 30 days. For an F-1 student this happens on passing the substantial presence test after the 5-calendar-year exemption.
abroad.taxAtSource: US federal: 0% on bank deposit interest paid to a nonresident alien when it is not effectively connected with a US trade or business (IRC 871(i)(2)(A)). A valid W-8BEN is required. Reporting on Form 1042-S applies when the NRA lives in a country listed in Rev. Proc. 2024-42. Without a valid certification, BofA states that backup or FATCA withholding applies.

assumptions: SLATE assumes a Bank of America account is kept after its holder moves abroad unless the destination is sanctioned. No residence-based closure clause is published, but the bank keeps a general discretion to close without advance notice.
SLATE found no official Bank of America 'moving abroad' FAQ. Third-party sites say BofA keeps expat accounts open, but SLATE does not treat that as published policy.

us-wells-fargo.conditions: Domestic case: kept with no special condition while the student lives in New Haven. For a customer who later moves abroad, the Deposit Account Agreement (eff. July 28, 2026) has no clause that closes accounts because of foreign residence. Its 'Change of address' clause only requires prompt notice. Published restrictions for customers living outside the US: 'You must have a current residence in the United States to send digital wire. Customers living in U.S. territories ... or other countries can't send digital wires' (Digital Wires FAQ). Customers outside the US who want to close an account must mail an Account Closure form notarized by an agency recognized by the US Embassy or Consulate. Wells Fargo's 2021 exit of non-US-resident clients is documented for its brokerage and private-bank arms by third parties. It is not stated in the deposit agreement. The bank-initiated closure clause: 'We may close your account at any time.'
us-wells-fargo.usResidentPolicy: Not applicable as a restriction (US bank). Deposit Account Agreement: 'U.S. Treasury regulations require us to determine the tax residency of all customers ... by obtaining a Form W-9 from all U.S. taxpayers and a type of Form W-8 from all foreign customers.' Without a valid W-8, Wells Fargo applies 30% withholding or treats the customer as an uncertified US taxpayer subject to backup withholding.

abroad.card: International purchase transaction fee: 3% of the US dollar amount for each purchase in a foreign currency that a network converts into dollars (Consumer Account Fee and Information Schedule, eff. July 28, 2026). Premier Checking waives it.
abroad.atm: Non-Wells Fargo ATM cash withdrawal, international: $5 each. A teller cash disbursement abroad costs 3% of the US dollar amount.
abroad.outgoing: Outgoing international wire: digital wire in US currency $30, digital wire in foreign currency no fee, branch wire $40 (Consumer Account Fee and Information Schedule eff. July 28, 2026; Consumer and Business Fees page eff. Sept 11, 2026).
abroad.incoming: Incoming international wire: no fee (consumer).
abroad.fxMargin: 'The exchange rate used when Wells Fargo converts one currency to another is set at our sole discretion, and it includes a markup.' No margin percentage is published.
abroad.days: 'For international wires, delivery times vary, depending on your recipient's country' (Digital Wires FAQ). Same-day cutoff is 2:20 pm PT.
abroad.opening: Online opening requires 'a physical U.S. address', an SSN or ITIN and a mobile number. 'If you're ... a non-permanent U.S. resident, you'll need to make an appointment to apply in person.' A non-US citizen without a US TIN must show a government ID evidencing nationality or residence, such as a passport. Wells Fargo publishes no opening for someone who lives abroad.
abroad.kyc: CIP (31 CFR 1020.220) at opening. US taxpayers give a W-9 and TIN; until Wells Fargo has them, it applies backup withholding. Foreign individuals give a W-8BEN; without a valid W-8 the bank applies 30% withholding or treats the customer as an uncertified US person. The customer must notify address changes promptly. Wells Fargo publishes no specific KYC-refresh cycle.
abroad.taxAtSource: US federal: 0% on bank deposit interest paid to a nonresident alien when it is not effectively connected (IRC 871(i)(2)(A)), with a valid W-8BEN. Reported on Form 1042-S for residents of the countries in Rev. Proc. 2024-42. Wells Fargo's agreement states 30% withholding if no valid W-8 is on file.

assumptions: SLATE assumes a Wells Fargo deposit account is kept after its holder moves abroad but loses digital wires. The reported 2021 non-US-resident exits are attributed to Wells Fargo's brokerage and private bank, not to the deposit agreement, so SLATE does not model them as a deposit closure.
SLATE assumes no fixed notice before a Wells Fargo-initiated closure, because the agreement says only 'We may close your account at any time.'

us-citi.conditions: Domestic case: kept with no special condition while the student lives in New Haven. For a customer who later moves abroad, the Consumer Deposit Account Agreement (U.S. Markets, eff. Nov 20, 2025) states that its products and services 'are not offered to individual residents in Europe, including the European Union, European Economic Area, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, and similar countries.' It also states: 'If your country of residence is other than the United States or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, you acknowledge that you are responsible for ... all laws, regulations, and rules applicable to your accounts ... including any tax, foreign exchange, or capital controls.' So keeping an account while resident abroad is contemplated, but not for residents of Europe or 'similar countries'. A change of residential address does not change the Governing State. The bank-initiated closure clause: 'We may close your account at any time with or without cause. We will notify you that we closed your account when required by law.'
us-citi.usResidentPolicy: Not applicable as a restriction (US bank). 'U.S. persons are required to furnish or have a valid Form W-9 ... Foreign individuals are required to furnish or have a valid Form W-8BEN.'

abroad.card: Foreign exchange fee of 3% of the transaction amount for each international debit card purchase or ATM withdrawal (including at proprietary Citibank ATMs) made in a currency other than USD outside the 50 states and territories. Waived for Citigold Private Client, Citigold and Citi Priority.
abroad.atm: Non-Citi ATM fee: $2.50 (Regular Checking and Access Checking) when a Network ATM outside the surcharge-free network is used, plus the 3% foreign exchange fee on foreign-currency withdrawals, plus any operator fee. Waived in Relationship Tiers.
abroad.outgoing: Standard fee column of the Wire / Intra Citi Transfer Fee Chart (column alignment read from PDF text extraction): outgoing online international wire in USD $35; online international wire in foreign currency waived; international wire through other channels (branch/banker) $45.
abroad.incoming: Incoming domestic and international wire: $15 (standard). Waived for Citigold.
abroad.fxMargin: 'Citibank's exchange rate includes a commission for the conversion service' (Citibank Global Transfer and foreign currency wires). No margin percentage is published.
abroad.days: Citibank Global Transfers to US Citi accounts are credited immediately. For international transfers, not published as a number.
abroad.opening: Online opening on citi.com requires the applicant to be a US citizen or US resident alien, with a physical US address and an SSN or ITIN (Citi account-opening guidance, seen via search snippet). Citi serves non-residents through separate units: International Personal Bank (ipbus.citi.com) and Citigold/Citi Private Bank. SLATE did not research their minimums. The US Markets agreement says it is 'not ... an offer ... to individuals outside of the United States'.
abroad.kyc: CIP (31 CFR 1020.220) at opening. W-9 for US persons, W-8BEN for foreign individuals. A customer resident outside the US accepts responsibility for local tax, FX and capital-control rules. Citi publishes no specific KYC-refresh cycle.
abroad.taxAtSource: US federal: 0% on bank deposit interest paid to a nonresident alien when it is not effectively connected (IRC 871(i)(2)(A)), with a valid W-8BEN. Reported on Form 1042-S for residents of the countries in Rev. Proc. 2024-42. Citi's agreement says bonuses paid to non-resident aliens are reported on Form 1042-S.

assumptions: SLATE assumes a Citi account is kept after its holder moves abroad unless the new residence is in Europe (EU/EEA/Switzerland/UK) or a 'similar country'. Citi says it does not offer its US-market products to those residents, and SLATE treats that as a likely closure.
SLATE reads Citi's standard-tier wire fees from a PDF table whose columns were scrambled by text extraction. The values $15, $35, waived and $45 were aligned by row order and are marked as such.

us-capital-one.conditions: Domestic case: kept with no special condition while the student lives in New Haven. Published eligibility for 360 Checking: 'available to United States citizens or lawful permanent residents with a U.S. physical address located in one of the 50 United States or Washington, D.C., or with military addresses (APO or FPO)', plus an SSN or ITIN and a US mobile number (360 Checking disclosures, dated 5/20/2026). For a customer who later moves abroad, the Rules Governing Deposit Accounts (eff. Sept 16, 2026) have no foreign-residence clause, but the product eligibility assumes a US physical address. The bank-initiated closure clause: 'Bank may close any Account in Bank's sole discretion at any time, for any or no reason and without notice to Customer.'
us-capital-one.usResidentPolicy: Not applicable as a restriction (US bank). Capital One's NRA Additional Information Form ('Must accompany Forms W-8BEN') is required from nonresident aliens with a US address or US phone. One listed reason is 'I am a student at a U.S. educational institution and hold the appropriate visa (e.g. F, J, M, or Q visas)'. If the form is not provided, 24% withholding can apply.

abroad.card: 360 Checking and MONEY: 'no additional fees when you use your debit card abroad (any transaction made in a foreign currency or that is classified as a cross-border transaction).' Non-360 products: $2 plus 3% at an international ATM.
abroad.atm: 360 Checking: no Capital One fee abroad (the ATM operator may charge). Non-360 products: $2 plus 3% of the total transaction amount outside the US, Puerto Rico and the USVI.
abroad.outgoing: 'At this time, you can only send international wires through our branch locations.' Fee: $40 (Capital One help center). A domestic outgoing wire costs $30.
abroad.incoming: 360 Checking: no incoming wire fee is listed in its disclosures. Capital One's SWIFT code is HIBKUS44. 'International wires may take 3–5 business days to arrive and be deposited to your account.'
abroad.fxMargin: Rules Governing Deposit Accounts: foreign checks are 'exchanged at the Bank's current daily exchange rate'. 'Bank's Fees only cover its own costs for international wire transfers; additional costs or fees ... may be incurred.' No margin is published.
abroad.days: Outgoing international: 'may take up to 10 business days to be deposited to the recipient's account.' Incoming international: 3–5 business days.
abroad.opening: Not from abroad: 360 Checking requires a US physical address in the 50 states or DC (or APO/FPO), an SSN or ITIN and a US mobile number. The published eligibility names US citizens and lawful permanent residents. Capital One's NRA form shows it does hold accounts for nonresident aliens with US addresses, such as F-1 students, but it publishes no non-resident opening channel.
abroad.kyc: CIP (31 CFR 1020.220) at opening, with a street address (no PO box). US persons give a W-9 SSN/ITIN. Nonresident aliens give a W-8BEN plus the NRA Additional Information Form explaining the US address or phone (an F/J/M/Q student is a listed reason). This must be given again on recertification or any change of circumstance affecting foreign status, otherwise 24% withholding applies.
abroad.taxAtSource: US federal: 0% on bank deposit interest paid to a nonresident alien when it is not effectively connected (IRC 871(i)(2)(A)), with a valid W-8BEN. Reported on Form 1042-S for residents of the countries in Rev. Proc. 2024-42. Capital One's NRA form warns of 24% withholding if its documentation is missing.

assumptions: SLATE assumes a Capital One 360 account is at risk once its holder no longer has a US physical address, because the product's published eligibility requires one. No closure clause or grace period is published, so SLATE treats retention abroad as conditional.

SLATE assumes an F-1 student who already holds a Capital One account (with W-8BEN and NRA form) keeps it while in New Haven. The published 360 eligibility wording names citizens and permanent residents only, so SLATE does not model new 360 openings by F-1 students.

ca-rbc.conditions: RBC's Personal Deposit Account Agreement (s.24 'Address or Residency') requires the client to 'immediately notify us' of any change of address or residency, and to report any change of tax residency 'within 30 days'; 'failure to provide a valid self-certification under FATCA or CRS will result in the temporary restraint of your Account until such time as it is provided'. Nothing in the agreement closes the account because the holder moves abroad and there is no separate non-resident account type. RBC can still close the account at its discretion: s.6 lets it 'suspend, freeze, or restrict access to, restrain, block, or terminate your right to use your Account ... for any reason in our discretion, including, without notice' (e.g. unsatisfactory operation, contrary to policies, required by law). After 12 months without transactions the account goes inactive; a $0 inactive account is closed without notice, and the balance goes to the Bank of Canada after 10 years.
ca-rbc.nonResidentFee: not published (no non-resident surcharge appears in the fee schedule; ordinary plan fees apply, e.g. RBC Advantage Banking $12.95 CAD/month, waived for students; RBC Day to Day Banking $4.00 CAD/month)
ca-rbc.usResidentPolicy: Not published as a refusal. The agreement explains FATCA (the CRA shares information with the IRS on accounts of U.S. persons, 'a citizen or a resident of the United States') and requires a U.S. TIN when FATCA applies ('If you fail to provide a U.S. TIN when required under FATCA, you may be assessed a penalty of $100 by the CRA'). An account with a missing self-certification is restrained, not described as closed. RBC also markets RBC Bank (U.S.) accounts to Canadians who study in the US, which assumes that keeping the Canadian RBC account is normal.

abroad.card: Purchases with the Client Card abroad go through Interac Debit Cross Border, which costs $1.00 CAD per purchase on RBC Advantage Banking and RBC Day to Day Banking (VIP is free). The amount is also converted 'at an exchange rate of 2.5% over the Interbank Spot Rate as defined by Interac Corp.' (footnote 10, PDA Disclosures, August 3, 2026). The fee table in the PDF extracts imperfectly, so the per-item mapping is SLATE's reading of it.
abroad.atm: PLUS Access Fee: $3.00 CAD per withdrawal in Canada or the U.S., and $5.00 CAD outside Canada or the U.S. (RBC Advantage Banking and Day to Day Banking; RBC VIP Banking free). Cash and any third-party ATM fees are converted 'at an exchange rate which is 2.5% above the benchmark rate set by the payment card company' (footnote 9). ATM operator surcharges are extra.
abroad.outgoing: Outgoing wire: 'starting at' $45.00 CAD from a CAD account ($45.00 USD from a USD account), plus a $35.00 surcharge if no IBAN is given for an IBAN country, which does not apply to the US. Intermediary or receiving banks may charge more.
abroad.incoming: Incoming wire from another financial institution worldwide: free under $50 CAD/USD; 'starting at' $17.00 CAD (or $17.00 USD into a USD account) for larger amounts.
abroad.fxMargin: A rate RBC sets. The agreement says RBC converts 'at the exchange rate we set for that type of transaction at the time we complete the transaction' and 'the exchange rate used may result in revenue being earned by us on the conversion'. The margin is not published.
abroad.days: RBC International Money Transfer: 'typically, the recipient can access the funds within 2 business days', and up to 7 business days. Wire timing is not published.
abroad.opening: RBC's own published route for a non-resident is narrow. Its US affiliate RBC Bank (U.S.) markets a Direct or Premium Student Bundle to Canadian students to 'set up your bank account and credit card in the U.S. before you start your studies' (offer runs to October 31, 2026). Opening a new Canadian RBC account while living in the US is not published for a non-resident who is not moving to Canada. The FCAC says that a person living in another country may be able to open an account but may need to attend in person (see countries.CA).
abroad.kyc: The agreement (s.24) requires immediate notice of any change of address or residency, and notice of a change in tax residency within 30 days. RBC must collect a TIN for every jurisdiction of tax residence ('If you are not eligible or unable to obtain a foreign TIN, you must provide a reasonable explanation'). A missing FATCA or CRS self-certification restrains the account. Under the PCMLTFA, RBC may adopt client-identification policies 'more rigorous than statutory or regulatory requirements'. A US-resident holder would give a self-certification naming US tax residency and a US TIN (SSN or ITIN). A W-9 or W-8BEN is not named in the RBC deposit agreement.
abroad.taxAtSource: 0% in general: Canada does not withhold Part XIII tax on arm's-length interest such as bank-deposit interest. The 25% rate in ITA 212(1)(b) applies only to non-arm's-length interest and participating debt interest. See countries.CA.

assumptions: SLATE assumes RBC keeps a Canadian account open for a holder who moves to New Haven, provided the holder reports the move and the change of tax residency within 30 days, because the agreement requires notice and self-certification but contains no clause that closes an account because the holder lives abroad.
SLATE assumes RBC Online Banking and the Mobile app keep working from the US, since RBC publishes no geographic restriction and markets cross-border banking to students in the US.
SLATE assumes RBC can close the account at any time without notice under s.6, so the account carries a small discretionary closure risk rather than a fixed notice period.

ca-td.conditions: TD's Financial Services Terms (effective August 10, 2026) require the customer to 'contact us right away' about changes to the mailing address and other contact information, and to 'respond to any requests for information from us in the allotted time'. The terms contain no clause that closes an account because the holder lives outside Canada and no non-resident account type. TD may 'close your Account with or without notifying you' (s.2.3) for listed reasons that include 'Your Account operates in a way that we find unsatisfactory or contrary to our policies', 'We seek to protect your or our interests', 'We are required to do so by law' and 'Your Account has no activity for a certain period of time'. TD also sells a Canadian-domiciled U.S. Daily Interest Chequing Account and runs Cross-Border Banking with TD Bank in the US, which assumes customers who stay with TD Canada while in the US.
ca-td.nonResidentFee: not published (the fee guide shows no non-resident surcharge; the TD Student Chequing Account is $0.00 a month and stays available after 23 'with proof of enrollment in full-time post-secondary education')
ca-td.usResidentPolicy: Not published as a refusal. TD's Tax Residency Self-Certification for individuals asks whether the client is a U.S. citizen or U.S. resident for tax purposes and, if so, for a U.S. TIN. TD publishes FATCA/Part XVIII information and runs a Cross-Border Banking service aimed at Canadians who 'work, live, vacation or study' in the US.

abroad.card: TD Access Card (Visa Debit) purchase in a foreign currency: converted at the rate set by Visa International, plus 'a fee equal to 3.5% of the purchase amount after conversion to Canadian dollars' (About Our Accounts, effective March 5, 2026).
abroad.atm: Non-TD ATM: $3.00 CAD in the USA or Mexico and $5.00 CAD in any other foreign country, with no service fee on the TD All-Inclusive Banking Plan (it also waives the US fee, as do TD Unlimited Chequing and a high-balance TD High Interest Saving Account). In addition, 3.5% of the converted amount, including any ATM provider fee. TD ATMs in the US are part of TD's network ('Access to over 4,000 TD ATMs across Canada and US').
abroad.outgoing: Wire payment by visiting a branch to a non-TD account 'within Canada or internationally': $50.00 CAD ($16.00 to another TD Canada Trust account). Fees are in CAD or the CAD equivalent. Other banks may charge more.
abroad.incoming: Receive a wire payment: $17.50, charged in USD if the funds arrive in USD and in CAD otherwise.
abroad.fxMargin: A rate TD sets: 'you will be purchasing the other currency from us at the exchange rate we set'. For TD Global Transfer the rate is 'set and disclose[d] to you before you complete the transfer'. The margin is not published.
abroad.days: not published for wires or TD Global Transfer. TD-Canada-to-TD-Bank-US transfers made in EasyWeb post after about 30 minutes ('Funds will not be debited ... until the transaction is processed (30 minutes after submission)').
abroad.opening: TD's own cross-border page says that a US TD Bank account 'can only be opened in a TD Bank, America's Most Convenient Bank location'. An aggregator (not TD) says the TD New to Canada package can be started online but must be completed at a branch in Canada.

II inciso a) on interest paid to non-residents by credit institutions (instituciones de crédito); the US-Mexico treaty art. 11(2)(b) caps interest paid by banks to a US-resident individual at 10%, so the lower domestic 4.9% governs. Contract: 'EL BANCO deducirá, retendrá y enterará el impuesto que corresponda.' See countries.MX.

gb-barclays.conditions: Barclays publishes that to keep Barclays accounts open 'you and anyone you share an account with need to live in the UK' and all account addresses must be in the UK. The only published exceptions: (a) UK Crown employee or spouse/civil partner of one; (b) the non-UK address is for someone who manages the account (power of attorney, accountant, lawyer); (c) 'You're outside the UK on a temporary basis for six months or less and will be moving back to the UK.' If the address is outside the UK, Barclays says it will contact the customer to close the current/savings account. Its student FAQ says accounts stay open while the customer is UK-based and close once they leave. A Yale student (multi-year stay) fits none of the exceptions. Notice: Barclays' page says only it will 'give you as much notice as we can'; the personal terms' general clause (quoted in Financial Ombudsman decisions) lets Barclays close a personal account on at least two months' notice. For accounts opened on or after 28 April 2026 the statutory minimum is 90 days (see countries.GB). Alternative: Barclays International Banking (offshore) needs at least £100,000 in savings/investments (£250,000 for a relationship manager).
gb-barclays.usResidentPolicy: Not published for UK retail accounts. Residence outside the UK is itself the closure ground, so a US resident is closed out whatever their nationality. Nothing is published about refusing US persons (citizens) who live in the UK.

abroad.card: 2.99% non-sterling transaction fee on purchases, cash withdrawals and refunds in a currency other than sterling (Barclays tariff for personal customers, correct as at 1 June 2025).
abroad.atm: 2.99% non-sterling transaction fee (same fee as purchases). No separate cash fee is listed in the 1 June 2025 tariff.
abroad.outgoing: £0 for international payments made in the Barclays app or Online Banking; £25 in branch or by Telephone Banking. An optional overseas bank charge of £4, £6 or £12 can be paid so the recipient pays no fees. A £3 USD cover charge applies only to US dollars sent to an account outside the US.
abroad.incoming: £0 for an international payment of £100.00 or less; £6 for £100.01 or more (£0 for SEPA or euro from the EEA).
abroad.fxMargin: Barclays Reference Exchange Rate (set by Barclays, based on market rates) plus a currency conversion charge of no more than 2.75% for Personal and Premier customers, reducing above £25,000.
abroad.days: To accounts outside the UK/EEA in other currencies: 'varies depending on the currency or country'. The international payments page says 'Most payments arrive within one to two working days.'
abroad.opening: No for a UK retail current account: the living-outside-the-UK policy requires a UK address. Barclays points non-residents to Barclays International Banking (offshore), minimum £100,000 (or currency equivalent) in savings or investments. Whether Barclays International accepts US residents is not published in the sources read.
abroad.kyc: Barclays publishes that all account addresses must be in the UK, so registering a US address triggers closure. No published W-9/W-8BEN procedure for retail customers was found. UK banks report under the UK–US FATCA IGA and the CRS through HMRC (see countries.GB).
abroad.taxAtSource: None. UK banks have paid interest gross since 6 April 2016 (HMRC). See countries.GB.

SLATE assumes a Yale student on a multi-year course does not qualify for the 'six months or less' temporary-absence exception, so Barclays closes the account once a US address is registered.

gb-lloyds.conditions: Lloyds' personal banking terms (dated 13 July 2026, per search snippet) say that if you move abroad and no longer live in the UK, Lloyds 'may not be able to keep your account open or continue offering you the same level of service or account benefits'. Customers moving abroad must tell Lloyds and change their address, in branch per Lloyds help. Lloyds-site snippets say overseas-addressed customers keep receiving statements and cards, that Lloyds offers new savings accounts only to UK residents, and that out-of-policy non-UK-resident savings accounts are closed and repaid by sterling cheque. In 2020–21 Lloyds Banking Group closed UK accounts of customers resident in some EU countries for Brexit licensing reasons; that was country-specific and did not cover the US. Notice: Financial Ombudsman decisions quote Lloyds' terms as giving 'at least 2 months' notice when ending an agreement, and record a 65-day closure notice to a customer living abroad. Lloyds' site blocked automated fetching (Cloudflare error 1007), so this rests on search snippets of lloydsbank.com pages and PDFs.
gb-lloyds.usResidentPolicy: Nothing published for UK retail accounts. Lloyds Bank International publishes that its International Plus Account is not available to US, Canadian or Hong Kong residents 'due to regulatory requirements'. Its terms note that 'a US citizen is treated as US tax resident' for reporting.

abroad.card: Per a lloydsbank.com travel page (search snippet, not fetched): 2.99% foreign currency transaction fee on standard debit cards, plus a £0.50 foreign currency purchase fee per purchase (not for euro purchases in the EEA/UK). No fee on Club, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Premier, Student and Graduate cards. Travel Smart (£7/week, up to 6 weeks a year) waives the fees.
abroad.atm: Per the same snippet: 2.99% foreign currency transaction fee plus a £1.50 foreign currency cash fee on standard debit cards; none on Club, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Premier, Student and Graduate cards. Not verified by a direct fetch.
abroad.outgoing: Per Lloyds help pages (search snippet): £9.50 for non-euro international payments sent online or in the app, always on SHA (shared) charges; no Lloyds fee for euro payments. Optional OUR charges: Zone 1 (USA, Canada, non-EEA Europe) £12 correspondent fee. Daily limit £100,000 in app/online. Some aggregators claim app payments are now free; this is not confirmed by a Lloyds page.
abroad.incoming: Per Lloyds snippet: £2 for an electronic payment from outside the UK up to £100; £7 over £100; none for euro from the UK/EEA/SEPA.
abroad.fxMargin: not published in any page that could be read (Lloyds sets its own exchange rate).
abroad.days: not published in any page that could be read.
abroad.opening: No for a UK retail account: a UK address is required. Lloyds Bank International (offshore, Isle of Man/Jersey) offers International Current / Premier International accounts in GBP, EUR and USD, subject to an eligibility checker that excludes some countries. The International Plus Account excludes US residents. Not verified directly because the site blocked fetching.
abroad.kyc: Must tell Lloyds of a move abroad and change the address (in branch, per Lloyds help snippet). Lloyds Bank International terms say regulators may be informed of assets/interest depending on tax residence, 'a US citizen is treated as US tax resident'. No published W-9/W-8BEN procedure for retail customers was found.
abroad.taxAtSource: None. Interest paid gross since 6 April 2016 (HMRC). See countries.GB.

gb-natwest.conditions: NatWest publishes no closure rule for customers moving outside the EEA. Its Brexit hub says that for EEA-resident customers 'our aim is to continue to provide you with the same service ... where we are permitted to do so', and that it closed accounts of many Netherlands residents because of Dutch law. Its support centre (search snippet) says that 'in most cases, there will be no change to the products and services you use if you move abroad', but packaged-account benefits (e.g. insurance) cannot be used while living overseas. Customers must not keep a UK address on file if not UK-resident. Notice: 'As stated in our Terms and Conditions, we're required to give you 60 days' notice of our intention to close your account.' Expat alternative: NatWest International (Jersey) International Select account, minimum balance £25,000, £8 monthly fee, residents of eligible countries only.
gb-natwest.usResidentPolicy: not published. Nothing found on refusing or closing accounts of US residents or US persons. Whether the US is eligible for NatWest International's International Select account is not stated on its page (it uses an eligibility checker).

abroad.card: 2.75% Non-Sterling Transaction Fee on debit card purchases in a foreign currency; none on Reward, Reward Silver, Reward Platinum, Premier Select, Premier Reward, Premier Reward Black and Black accounts.
abroad.atm: 2.75% Non-Sterling Transaction Fee on overseas ATM withdrawals, which still applies on the fee-free reward/premier accounts. A search snippet also mentions a 3% (min £3) 'Cash Fee', which appears to be for credit cards and not debit.
abroad.outgoing: 'There is no fee for sending an international payment online' (app or Online Banking). The receiving bank may charge. A third-party summary (not official) says urgent online payments cost £15 and branch/telephone non-euro payments £22.
abroad.incoming: No fee for euro payments. Non-euro under £100: £1. Over £100: £7.
abroad.fxMargin: When currency conversion is needed, a margin that 'will not be more than 3.25%'. Live rates shown before payment.
abroad.days: Non-euro payments to the USA: 1-3 business days, 16:00 UK cut-off.
abroad.opening: No for a NatWest UK retail current account (a UK residential address is required). NatWest International (Jersey law) International Select: aged 18+, resident in an eligible country, £25,000 minimum balance, £8/month. US eligibility not stated.
abroad.kyc: NatWest says you cannot use a UK address as your place of residence to keep an account open unless you are UK-resident, so the US address must be registered. No published W-9/W-8BEN procedure for retail customers was found. Reporting under the UK–US FATCA IGA and the CRS goes through HMRC (countries.GB).
abroad.taxAtSource: None. Interest paid gross since 6 April 2016 (HMRC). See countries.GB.

gb-hsbc.conditions: HSBC UK, 'Leaving the UK checklist', on keeping the UK account: 'Although you're allowed to do so, it only makes sense if you'll be using the account regularly'. Dormant accounts may be frozen or closed. Some account features may not be available while living outside the UK, and HSBC says to 'speak to your bank about your plans before you move and check any residency requirements'. An HSBC UK notice (search snippet, about EEA residents under CRD6 Article 21c) says existing products 'will remain unchanged' but 'While you live outside the UK, HSBC UK Bank plc won't offer you any other ... products or services'. Terms (effective 6 July 2026): HSBC may close accounts 'by giving you at least two months' notice or any longer period required by regulation'. It may close straight away if, among other things, 'You haven't given us information that we've asked for about your tax situation' or 'You weren't entitled, or aren't entitled any longer, to ... have your account'. A Basic Bank Account may be closed on two months' notice if 'You're no longer legally resident in the UK.'
gb-hsbc.usResidentPolicy: not published for HSBC UK retail. The terms say that if HSBC believes the customer may be tax resident in another country it may disclose information to HMRC, which may pass it to another government under an agreement. HSBC Expat lists the USA among countries where it can help open accounts. Its FAQ says nothing about US-person restrictions.

abroad.atm: Premier / Premier MyAccount: 2.75%. All other accounts: 2.75% plus a fee of 2.00% (minimum £1.75, maximum £5.00) (T&Cs effective 6 July 2026).
abroad.outgoing: Free by Branch, Telephone, Mobile or Online Banking for sending money from an HSBC account to a non-HSBC account in any currency outside the UK. £17 by post. Intermediary banks may deduct charges. OUR/SHA/BEN options. (T&Cs effective 6 July 2026.)
abroad.incoming: £5 for receiving money in a foreign currency; £5 for receiving pounds sterling from outside the UK (T&Cs effective 6 July 2026).
abroad.fxMargin: HSBC Exchange Rate, 'based on the foreign currency market for each currency we offer', shown in Online/Mobile Banking before payment. The margin is not stated in the T&Cs. Global Money Account: conversion charge 2.2% for £0–£50,000, tiered down to 1.3% above £100,000.

Expat route: HSBC Expat (Jersey), aged 18+, resident of an eligible country, and either £75,000 saved/invested with HSBC Expat within 3 months, a £120,000 salary paid in (per search snippet), or existing HSBC Premier status elsewhere (FAQ: Premier plus £10,000).
abroad.kyc: Terms: HSBC may close immediately if the customer hasn't given information requested 'about your tax situation'. If HSBC believes the customer may be tax resident elsewhere it may disclose to HMRC for onward exchange. The checklist says to tell HMRC about leaving the UK and to check residency requirements with the bank. No published W-9/W-8BEN procedure for HSBC UK retail was found.

gb-santander.conditions: Santander UK General Terms (effective 31 October 2025, notice of variation for 28 April 2026): 'For all accounts you must be a UK resident ... If you move abroad (or plan to), you must let us know. From time to time, we may also check if you still meet those requirements.' The moving-abroad page says: 'We can currently service existing products. However, if there is a change in the regulatory position, or there is political uncertainty within the country in which you're living, we will contact you directly and let you know your options.' While abroad, no new or increased overdrafts, cashback only on UK Direct Debits, and no new products ('To apply for any Santander UK plc product, you need to be a resident of the UK'). Change of address to overseas is by a posted form with ID and proof of address. Financial Ombudsman decisions record Santander closing accounts of customers living abroad for not meeting the UK-residence eligibility, or because the country of residence was high-risk. Notice: the current terms say 2 months for a payment account. The notice of variation says that from 28 April 2026 'we'll give you 90 days' notice'.
gb-santander.usResidentPolicy: not published. The terms say Santander may share information with HMRC for other tax authorities and the customer must supply requested documents within 30 days.

abroad.card: 2.95% foreign currency conversion fee on debit card payments in foreign currency (standard accounts). 0% on Santander Edge, Edge Up, Edge Explorer and Private (v2) accounts (Interest rates and fees for current accounts, correct as at 17 December 2025).
abroad.atm: Cash withdrawal fee: not charged. 2.95% foreign currency conversion fee (0% on Edge/Edge Up/Edge Explorer). Withdrawals at Santander ATMs in the USA (and Germany, Poland, Portugal, Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Mexico, Puerto Rico, Uruguay) with a Santander debit card: no cash withdrawal fee. The conversion-fee row reads 'Fee not charged' in the PDF's text order, but the table layout is ambiguous.
abroad.outgoing: £25 for a standard electronic international transfer (non-urgent SEPA euro: no fee). Santander Edge, Edge Up and Edge Explorer holders do not pay the £25 international transfer/CHAPS fee.
abroad.incoming: No fee for receiving a foreign currency electronic payment (Santander international payments page, per search snippet; the fetched page did not show receiving fees).
abroad.fxMargin: Mark-up on the exchange rate: 3% up to £10,000; 2% £10,001–£50,000; 1% £50,001 and higher.
abroad.days: US dollar transfers: 'usually within 4 working days' (same working day within UK/US).
abroad.opening: No. 'To apply for any Santander UK plc product, you need to be a resident of the UK'. Terms: 'For all accounts you must be a UK resident.'
abroad.kyc: Must tell Santander of a move abroad. Overseas address change by posted form with valid ID and proof of address (Santander Banking Operations, Sunderland SR43 4FP). Must supply tax-information documents within 30 days of request (terms). Santander may close immediately if information reasonably asked for more than once is not provided. Relies on CRS self-certification (Ombudsman decisions).

gb-nationwide.conditions: Nationwide's 'Living and working abroad' help page treats keeping a current account abroad as normal: change contact details to the new address, update the tax declaration, register the app before leaving. Its Brexit help (search snippet) says customers living permanently in the EU/EEA can generally continue to operate their accounts, but Nationwide cannot open new accounts, raise overdraft or credit limits, or extend borrowing. Its 'Moving your current account abroad' page covers EU/EEA moves and says closing the account is optional ('if you wish'). FlexPlus insurances do not apply outside the UK, but the £18 fee continues. Current Account terms (from 1 May 2025): Nationwide may block the account if 'we think you might be living outside the UK and it could increase the risk of fraud or other illegal activities on your account'. It can close at any time with 'at least two months' beforehand' notice. FlexBasic can be closed if the customer is no longer legally resident in the UK (search snippet of FlexBasic terms).
gb-nationwide.usResidentPolicy: not published. No statement on US residents or US persons was found.

abroad.atm: FlexAccount, FlexBasic, FlexDirect: 2.99% of the amount for foreign currency cash outside the UK. FlexPlus, FlexOne, FlexStudent, FlexGraduate: 0%.

abroad.days: Outside the EEA: 'longer than 4 working days, depending on the country and bank.'
abroad.opening: No. Nationwide (Brexit help, search snippet) cannot open a new account for a customer living abroad. Nationwide has no international/expat arm. Nationwide International (Isle of Man) is not used here.
abroad.kyc: Change contact details to the foreign address. 'If you've changed your address to or from a non-UK address, you'll need to update your tax declaration' (phone or branch). The terms allow Nationwide to close an account straight away if it needs information about 'your identity or your tax position' that hasn't been given. No published W-9/W-8BEN procedure was found.

ie-aib.conditions: AIB publishes no rule that closes a personal current account when the holder moves abroad. Its help pages let a customer change their address to a foreign country in the app or Internet Banking (Services > My Details > select country). The customer must tell AIB if their country of tax residence changes so that AIB can update its tax records. Some AIB products are limited to Irish residents: the Personal Sterling Current Account 'is only available to personal customers resident in Ireland'. Nothing equivalent is published for the euro personal current account. Bank-initiated closure: AIB's current account terms say AIB may close a personal current account by giving at least two months' notice (general termination clause; PSD2 framework-contract rule, S.I. 6/2018).
ie-aib.nonResidentFee: not published (no non-resident surcharge in the material read). From 1 July 2026 the standard personal current account fee is EUR 6 per month, replacing EUR 4.50 per quarter plus transaction fees. AIB Student and Student Plus accounts are exempt (AIB press release of 18 March 2026 and the 'Changes to fees and charges' page, read via search snippets because aib.ie returned HTTP 403).
ie-aib.usResidentPolicy: AIB does not publish a refusal or closure policy for US persons. It publishes FATCA obligations: AIB must report accounts held by US citizens and US tax residents to Irish Revenue, which exchanges the data with the IRS. Account opening requires a tax certification that establishes whether the holder is a US citizen and where they are tax resident. If the self-certification conflicts with other data held (for example a US address), AIB asks for a 'CRS/FATCA Reasonable Explanation Form' with supporting documents.

abroad.card: Debit card, non-euro point-of-sale purchase (including contactless): 1.75% of the euro value, minimum EUR 0.45, maximum EUR 11.00 (AIB Account Fees & Service Charges effective 1 July 2026, via search snippet; the PDF returned HTTP 403).
abroad.atm: Debit card, non-euro cash withdrawal: 2.5% of the euro value, plus a cash withdrawal commission of 1% of the euro value (minimum EUR 2.00, maximum EUR 6.00) (same source, via search snippet). The ATM owner may add its own surcharge.
abroad.outgoing: Outgoing non-SEPA international payment (for example USD to a US account), non-urgent: EUR 15 by electronic instruction, EUR 20 by paper instruction (AIB international payments FAQ / Schedule of International Transaction Charges, via search snippet). Intermediary and receiving banks may deduct their own charges.
abroad.incoming: Incoming international payment in a major currency from outside the EEA ('InPay Global'): no AIB fee up to EUR 127; EUR 6.35 above EUR 127 (aib.ie international payments page, via search snippet).
abroad.fxMargin: AIB's 'standard exchange rate' applies up to a threshold of the currency equivalent of EUR 70,000, and rates are posted on aib.ie. A search snippet from AIB's international payments material says a conversion charge 'of up to 1.4%' on the FX rate applies. The snippet may come from AIB's business/GB documents and is unverified for personal accounts.
abroad.days: USD payments: same business day at the earliest, subject to cut-off times (AIB international payments FAQ, via search snippet). EEA currency payments to the EEA take 1 to 4 business days.
abroad.opening: Possible, with conditions. AIB's identification requirements say a customer not resident in Ireland must provide one photographic ID and two proofs of address, and the names must match exactly. A non-resident must present in branch within 30 days of the account being opened. Photocopies are not accepted, and certified copies are required when posting. A tax (CRS/FATCA) certification is required at opening.
abroad.kyc: At opening, AIB takes photo ID, proof of address (two for non-residents) and a CRS/FATCA tax certification. The customer must notify AIB when their country of tax residence changes. AIB may then ask for a new tax certification and/or a Reasonable Explanation Form with documents from the new country of tax residence. A US person is reported to Revenue under FATCA, with a US TIN on the AIB tax certification. AIB uses its own certification form, not an IRS W-9 (no W-9 requirement found published). A non-US person resident in the US would certify US tax residency under CRS and give a TIN.
abroad.taxAtSource: Ireland: DIRT of 33% is withheld from deposit interest. It is not charged if every beneficial owner is non-resident and a non-resident declaration has been given to the bank (no joint holder resident in Ireland). Otherwise a US resident can reclaim DIRT under the Ireland–US double taxation agreement with Revenue Form IC5 (Revenue.ie).

assumptions: SLATE assumes AIB keeps a euro personal current account open for a customer who moves to the US and registers a US address, because AIB publishes a foreign-address change path and no residency condition for that account.
SLATE assumes no non-resident surcharge applies beyond the standard EUR 6 monthly fee, because none is published.

SLATE assumes a student who held an AIB Student/Student Plus account keeps the fee exemption only while AIB's eligibility for that account holds. AIB's eligibility rules for continuing study abroad were not found.

ie-bank-of-ireland.conditions: Bank of Ireland's help centre answers 'I live abroad, do I still have to use SCA?' with 'Yes, to ensure you can continue to use your cards for transactions in the EU or access your accounts online, you will need to be set up for SCA'. That answer presupposes customers living abroad keep their accounts. The 'Coming to Ireland' account (and some new accounts) must be updated to a Republic of Ireland address within 60 days of opening, or it is blocked and then closed if not updated within a further 30 days. That rule is a product-specific opening condition, not a rule for an established personal current account. Bank-initiated closure: the Personal Current Account terms say the bank may end the terms and close the account by giving two months' notice. It may also close immediately in listed cases (death, insolvency, breach).
ie-bank-of-ireland.nonResidentFee: not published (no non-resident surcharge found). The standard Personal Current Account maintenance fee is EUR 6 per month, charged on the last banking day of the month (Schedule of fees and charges for personal customers, effective 1 August 2025).
ie-bank-of-ireland.usResidentPolicy: Bank of Ireland publishes no refusal of US persons. Its FATCA/CRS self-certification form says the Group must report details of account holders who are US citizens and/or tax resident outside the Republic of Ireland. The customer agrees to tell the bank within 30 days if their tax residence or US citizenship changes, and to submit a new FATCA/CRS self-certification.

abroad.card: Debit card purchases in a foreign currency (including contactless): 2% of the transaction value, maximum EUR 11.43 per transaction. This is a 'cross-border handling charge' that includes the network fees and the currency-conversion margin (Schedule of fees and charges for personal customers, effective 1 August 2025).
abroad.atm: Debit card ATM cash withdrawal in a foreign currency: 3.5% of the transaction value, minimum EUR 3.17, maximum EUR 11.43 per transaction (same schedule). Government stamp duty of EUR 0.12 per ATM withdrawal also applies, capped at EUR 2.50 or EUR 5.00 a year depending on card type. The ATM owner may add a surcharge.
abroad.outgoing: 365 online InterPayplus credit transfer in foreign currency to a country outside the UK and EEA (for example USD to the USA): EUR 5 per payment plus a foreign exchange margin. The online daily limit is EUR 20,000 (EUR 10,000 to payees added by SMS code). For larger amounts, InterPay is done in branch. The customer cannot pay the payee bank's charges (OUR) on 365 payments outside the UK/EEA. (Schedule of International Transaction Charges and the 'sending money abroad' page.)
abroad.incoming: Inward cross-border payment in foreign currency (where a buy/sell rate applies): no charge for EUR 65 and under; EUR 5.00 per payment above EUR 65. Inward euro payments from outside the EEA/UK: no charge up to EUR 65, EUR 5.00 over 65 up to 150, EUR 7.50 over 150 up to 1,500, EUR 12.50 over 1,500.
abroad.fxMargin: Published maximum margins for GBP and USD on credit transfers, inward payments and similar: transactions up to EUR 10,000 carry a 4% spread (maximum 2.5% margin either side); EUR 10,000 to 70,000 carry a 3.5% spread (maximum 2.0% either side); over EUR 70,000 is negotiated (maximum 2%). Rates are based on current market rates and published daily on bankofireland.com.
abroad.days: 365 payments typically take 1 to 3 working days to the payee's bank.
abroad.opening: Bank of Ireland says a non-resident account cannot be opened online. The applicant must call to a branch with a valid passport or national identity card and a recent household bill as proof of address. A non-resident must also provide a character reference or financial history from their own bank. (In 2025 the bank launched a remote opening service for returning emigrants and international students coming to Ireland. It is aimed at people moving to Ireland, not at those leaving.)
abroad.kyc: Bank of Ireland asks for a FATCA and CRS self-certification (personal customers/sole traders form). The customer must notify the bank within 30 days of any change to tax residence or US citizenship and give a new self-certification. Reported data includes name, address, date of birth, tax residence countries, US citizenship, TINs, balance and gross interest. A US person certifies US citizenship and gives a US TIN on the bank's own form. No IRS W-9 requirement was found published. A non-US person resident in the US certifies US tax residency and gives a TIN.
abroad.taxAtSource: Ireland: DIRT of 33% applies unless every beneficial owner is non-resident and has given a non-resident declaration. If it is deducted, a US resident can reclaim it under the Ireland–US DTA with Form IC5 (Revenue.ie).

assumptions: SLATE assumes an established Bank of Ireland Personal Current Account stays open when the holder moves to the US, because the bank's help pages address customers who live abroad and publish no residency condition for that account.
SLATE assumes no non-resident surcharge beyond the EUR 6 monthly fee, because none is published.
SLATE assumes the 2023-dated international schedule (the latest the bank links) is still current, since its file was republished in May 2025.

ie-ptsb.conditions: PTSB requires applicants to be over 18 and resident in the Republic of Ireland to apply for a current account. Nothing found says an existing account is closed when the holder later moves abroad. PTSB's terms say that accounts held by non-residents (as defined by the Taxes Consolidation Act 1997) 'must be operated in accordance with statutory conditions and banking regulations' and that 'an additional form must be completed where a non-resident Account is required'. A customer who becomes non-resident may therefore need to complete a non-resident form, which is also the route to DIRT exemption. Bank-initiated closure: PTSB may close the account for any reason by giving at least two months' notice in writing (current account terms, via search snippet).
ie-ptsb.nonResidentFee: not published (no non-resident surcharge found). The Explore current account fee is EUR 8 per month, raised from EUR 6 in 2024. Student, Teen and Basic Payment Accounts and customers over 66 are exempt (PTSB fee FAQs, via search snippet).
ie-ptsb.usResidentPolicy: PTSB publishes no refusal of US persons. Its help pages say that a customer who is tax resident outside Ireland, holds multiple tax residencies or is a US person for tax purposes must give an Individual Self-Certification for FATCA and CRS, with supporting documents for each tax residence and TIN. PTSB must report these under CRS and FATCA to the Revenue Commissioners.

abroad.atm: ATM withdrawals in euro outside the EU and all non-euro withdrawals: 3.5% of the euro value, minimum EUR 3.17, maximum EUR 11.43 (PTSB fee document dated 18 October 2023 per search snippet, and current fee document via search snippet).

abroad.fxMargin: Card transactions: PTSB notifies EEA card currency-conversion charges as a percentage mark-up over the latest ECB euro reference rate (PTSB currency conversions page). The margin on international payments was not published in material that could be read.
abroad.days: not published in material read
abroad.opening: Not for a standard current account. PTSB's account pages say you must be over 18 and resident in the Republic of Ireland to apply. abroad.kyc: Account opening requires residence in Ireland, ID and proof of address. abroad.taxAtSource: Ireland: DIRT of 33% applies unless every beneficial owner is non-resident and has completed the non-resident declaration. If it is deducted, a US resident can reclaim it under the Ireland–US DTA with Form IC5 (Revenue.ie).

SLATE assumes incoming international payments cost the same as PTSB's published EUR 31.50 international credit-transfer charge only if a reading of the full PTSB charges document confirms it. Until then, SLATE treats the incoming fee as unknown.

is-landsbankinn.conditions: Landsbankinn publishes no rule that closes an account when the holder moves abroad. Its general terms require the customer to give name, kennitala, legal domicile and, where relevant, residence or tax domicile ('skattalega heimilisfesti'), and to keep them current. Its US-tax page requires everyone tax resident outside Iceland to register their foreign TIN with the bank. Access abroad depends on electronic ID (see access). Bank-initiated closure: 'Bankanum er heimilt að segja upp rammasamningi samkvæmt skilmálum þessum með tveggja mánaða uppsagnarfresti' (the bank may terminate the framework contract with two months' notice) (Almennir viðskiptaskilmálar 1532-06, June 2023, art. on termination). The bank may also end the relationship without notice for law or terms breaches, AML risk, reputational risk, or where the relationship 'does not fit its risk policy'.
is-landsbankinn.nonResidentFee: not published. The price list has no monthly current-account fee. The debit card annual fee is ISK 790 (free under 18), and debit card transactions cost ISK 18 each (free under 18; 150 free a year for ages 18–24) (Verðskrá effective 25 August 2026, items 2.1.1 and 2.5.1).
is-landsbankinn.usResidentPolicy: No refusal of US persons is published. Landsbankinn's 'Bandarísk skattamál' page says that under the Iceland–US information-exchange agreement (FATCA) the bank must in certain cases collect IRS W-forms. A W-9 is required from anyone born in the US, with US citizenship, or with US residence/address. A W-8BEN is required from non-US persons with US-source income. Forms are valid for three years.

abroad.card: Bank's mark-up on the VISA wholesale rate, all foreign card transactions: 2.30% (Verðskrá 25 Aug 2026, item 2.5.9), plus the ISK 18 debit transaction fee (2.5.1).
abroad.atm: Foreign cash withdrawal with a debit card: 1.00% commission (2.5.3), minimum ISK 800 (2.5.5 'Lágmarksþóknun vegna erlendrar úttektar reiðufjár'), plus the 2.30% VISA mark-up on currency conversion. The foreign ATM owner may add its own fee.
abroad.outgoing: Outgoing foreign payment (non-EUR/EEA, for example USD to the US), made in the online bank: ISK 900 (9.2.2.1). In branch or by the service centre: ISK 1,900 (9.2.2.2). The sender pays all recipient-side costs (OUR) for an extra ISK 3,000 (9.2.2.3). All foreign bank charges are passed on. EUR payments within the EEA made in the online bank/app: ISK 0 (9.1.2).
abroad.incoming: Incoming non-EEA/EUR payment: ISK 700 for receipt of payment instructions (9.2.1.1). A SWIFT MT/MX payment request credited to a Landsbankinn account is listed at ISK 400 (9.2.1.3). Incomplete information costs ISK 2,000 (9.2.1.2). Incoming EUR from the EEA: ISK 0 (9.1.1).
abroad.fxMargin: The bank's own posted exchange rates apply ('sjá gengi gjaldmiðla á hverjum tíma á www.landsbankinn.is'). No percentage margin on transfers is published.
abroad.days: not published in material read
abroad.opening: Landsbankinn's English FAQ says foreign nationals who are not resident in Iceland can open an account if they have an Icelandic ID number (kennitala). The bank cannot apply for the kennitala for you (apply via Registers Iceland). Original documents are required and processing can take up to two weeks. The passport copy must be certified by a notary or by a regulated EEA financial institution.
abroad.kyc: Under the AML law the bank carries out customer due diligence at onboarding, by periodic monitoring and per transaction, with identity proven by a passport, driving licence, ID card or qualified electronic ID. The customer must keep kennitala, domicile/tax domicile and contact data current. Anyone tax resident outside Iceland must register a foreign TIN (CRS). US persons give an IRS W-9 and non-US persons with US income give a W-8BEN, each valid for three years.
abroad.taxAtSource: Iceland: interest paid to a person resident abroad is taxable in Iceland and withheld at 12% when no tax treaty applies. The withholding is final. The Iceland–US treaty gives full exemption on interest. The exemption is claimed in advance on Skatturinn form RSK 5.42, or tax withheld is refunded on RSK 5.43 (Skatturinn guidance on island.is). The domestic capital income tax rate is 22%.

assumptions: SLATE assumes Landsbankinn keeps a current account open for a holder who moves to the US and registers a foreign tax residence and TIN, because no closure-on-emigration rule is published.

SLATE assumes a holder without an Icelandic passport (for example a foreign national who lived in Iceland) cannot set up e-ID remotely from the US, and so loses app/online access unless they already hold a working Auðkenni app or an Icelandic SIM e-ID.
SLATE assumes item 9.2.1.1 (ISK 700) is the fee for an incoming USD payment. The price list also shows ISK 400 for 9.2.1.3, and how the two lines combine is not published.

is-arion.conditions: Arion banki publishes no rule that closes an account when the holder moves abroad. Its general terms require the customer to give name, kennitala, address, residence, tax domicile and contact data (phone and email). If a customer has no access to digital channels and has failed to keep address, phone or email current, termination 'fer fram án tilkynningar' (happens without notice). Bank-initiated closure: 'Bankanum er heimilt að loka reikningi sem fellur undir gildissvið laga um greiðsluþjónustu með að minnsta kosti tveggja mánaða fyrirvara' (the bank may close an account under the Payment Services Act on at least two months' notice). The framework contract can likewise be terminated on two months' notice (Almennir viðskiptaskilmálar 18.7.1.15, 15 April 2026).
is-arion.nonResidentFee: not published. The price list has no monthly current-account fee. The debit card annual fee is ISK 950 (ISK 0 for age 23 and under), and debit card transactions cost ISK 19 each (ISK 0 for age 23 and under) (Verðskrá effective 7 May 2026, items 13.1, 13.1.1, 13.1.4, 13.1.5).
is-arion.usResidentPolicy: No refusal of US persons is published. The general terms list tax domicile and Tax Identification Number among the data used for customer risk assessment. A customer living abroad must give their tax residency, defined as the country where they lived 180 days in the last 360. No Arion-specific W-9 page was found.

abroad.card: Mark-up on the VISA wholesale rate on debit card transactions in a foreign currency: 2.50% (Verðskrá 7 May 2026, item 13.5), plus the ISK 19 debit transaction fee (13.1.4).
abroad.atm: Debit card cash withdrawal at a bank or ATM abroad: 1.00%, minimum ISK 790 (item 13.3.1), plus the 2.50% VISA mark-up on conversion. The foreign ATM owner may add a surcharge.
abroad.outgoing: Foreign payment made in the online bank or app (outside the EEA, for example to the US): ISK 895 (6.3.6). Made by Arion staff: ISK 2,495 (6.3.8). Express: ISK 3,500 (6.3.10). The sender pays foreign bank costs (OUR) for ISK 5,000 (6.3.11). All foreign bank costs and other outlays are charged separately. To the EEA via online bank/app: ISK 0 (6.3.7).
abroad.incoming: Paid into an Arion account from outside the EEA: ISK 650 (6.3.1). From the EEA: ISK 0 (6.3.2).
abroad.fxMargin: The bank's own exchange rates apply. No percentage margin is published for transfers. Price-list item 6.1 'Gjaldeyriskaup og innborganir á gjaldeyrisreikninga' covers notes only.
abroad.days: not published in material read
abroad.opening: Arion says the only requirement to open an account is an Icelandic ID number (kennitala), obtained from Registers Iceland (skra.is). An account can be opened in the Arion app with electronic ID, which in turn needs a kennitala and an e-ID-capable Icelandic SIM or the Auðkenni app.
abroad.kyc: Arion collects name, kennitala, address, residence, tax domicile, nationality, TIN, phone and email, and runs ongoing risk assessment under the AML law. Customers living abroad must declare their tax residency (180 days in the last 360) and give a TIN for CRS/FATCA reporting. No Arion page specifying W-9/W-8BEN was found.
abroad.taxAtSource: Iceland: 12% final withholding on interest paid to non-residents where no treaty applies. Full exemption under the Iceland–US treaty, claimed on RSK 5.42 (exemption) or RSK 5.43 (refund) (Skatturinn guidance on island.is).

assumptions: SLATE assumes Arion keeps a current account open for a holder who moves to the US and keeps address, phone and email current. Arion publishes no closure-on-emigration rule, but it can terminate without notice a customer with no digital access whose contact details lapse.
SLATE assumes a holder without an Icelandic passport cannot self-activate e-ID from the US and must rely on an existing Auðkenni app or phone support.

is-islandsbanki.conditions: Íslandsbanki publishes no rule that closes an account when the holder moves abroad, and it publishes services for customers living abroad (Auðkenni app, foreign mobile numbers). The customer must notify the bank of changes to information given for AML, FATCA or CRS purposes (general terms ch. 8). is-islandsbanki.nonResidentFee: not published. The price list has no monthly current-account fee. is-islandsbanki.usResidentPolicy: No refusal of US persons is published. The general terms say Íslandsbanki must ask specific due-diligence questions under FATCA and CRS. Customers tax resident outside Iceland must register their TIN with the bank ('Skráðu skattkennitölu þína (TIN)').

abroad.card: Mark-up on the Mastercard Inc. wholesale rate on card transactions in a foreign currency: 2.50% (Verðskrá 19 March 2026, item 1.6), plus the ISK 20 debit transaction fee.
abroad.atm: Cash withdrawal from an ATM abroad with a debit card: 2.00% (item 1.2), plus the 2.50% Mastercard mark-up on conversion. The ATM owner's own fees may be added.
abroad.outgoing: 'Aðrar erlendar greiðslur' (foreign payments other than EUR within the EEA, for example USD to the US): ISK 900 by self-service (online bank/app), ISK 2,790 by staff. abroad.incoming: Incoming foreign payment (non-EUR/EEA): ISK 680. If paid on to another bank: ISK 1,500. Incoming EUR from the EEA: ISK 0.
abroad.fxMargin: The exchange rate in force at the time of processing is applied (the bank's own posted rate). No percentage margin is published for transfers.
abroad.days: Íslandsbanki's foreign-transfer instructions say orders submitted outside the FX desk hours (09:15–15:30) are processed the next business day. Express payments ('flýtigreiðsla') reach the foreign bank the same day if ordered before the cut-off: 14:00 for Europe, 17:00 for the US and Canada. Standard delivery days to the US are not published.
abroad.opening: Íslandsbanki's 'Banking in Iceland' page says an account can only be opened with an Icelandic ID number (kennitala). With electronic ID it can be opened online, otherwise in a branch with a passport. A residence permit is required for customers from outside the EEA/EFTA. A non-EEA national living in the US therefore cannot open a new account.
abroad.kyc: Due diligence at onboarding and ongoing monitoring. The customer must notify changes to AML/FATCA/CRS information, and customers tax resident outside Iceland must register a TIN. No Íslandsbanki-specific W-9/W-8BEN instructions were found published. The general terms refer to FATCA questions at onboarding.
abroad.taxAtSource: Iceland: 12% final withholding on interest to non-residents absent a treaty. Full exemption under the Iceland–US treaty via RSK 5.42 (or refund via RSK 5.43). Íslandsbanki's own page 'Skattgreiðslur og skerðingar' covers withholding on savings.

assumptions: SLATE assumes Íslandsbanki keeps a current account open for a holder who moves to the US and registers a foreign TIN, because no closure-on-emigration rule is published and the bank publishes services aimed at customers living abroad.

SLATE assumes the residence-permit condition for non-EEA customers applies at opening only. Whether a non-EEA national's account is reviewed when their Icelandic residence permit lapses is not published.
SLATE assumes standard (non-express) transfers to the US arrive in 1–2 business days. The bank publishes only the cut-off times and the express same-day rule.
